workflow.option.commands.desc: The command each named check runs. A run counts as the check only when it runs that command.
workflow.option.commands.title: Check commands
workflow.option.commitMessage.desc: The message of the commit the merge queue makes: Combwork’s names the card’s key and title and adds Combwork’s trailers, and the branch’s own uses the message its commits have, with no card key or trailers, while Combwork still knows which card it merged.
workflow.option.commitMessage.title: Commit message
workflow.option.dependenciesDone.desc: A card that waits for others can’t start before their work is in.
workflow.option.dependenciesDone.none: Cards start only when the cards they wait for are done
workflow.option.dependenciesDone.title: Cards start only when the cards they wait for are merged
workflow.option.excluded.desc: The whole project folder, apart from these folders and files (.combwork always).
workflow.option.excluded.title: What the work is
workflow.option.fileLocks.desc: What happens when an agent tries to edit a file another agent in the same folder is editing.
workflow.option.fileLocks.title: File locks
workflow.option.finish.desc: When a card is done: once Combwork’s merge queue has merged it, once its agent has merged it and Combwork finds the work in the target branch, once it is committed, or whenever it is moved there.
workflow.option.finish.title: Who merges
workflow.option.focusedTests.desc: When a card is submitted, the project’s command chooses the tests its change needs (or its builder names them, for its reviewer to check), and the merge queue runs them on the merged result, moving the target only once they pass.
workflow.option.focusedTests.title: Each card’s focused tests pass on the merged result
workflow.option.folder.desc: In its own folder, a slot Combwork lends to the card or its lane, each card is built on a branch of its own, apart from other agents’ work; in the project folder, everyone sees each other’s unfinished changes.
workflow.option.folder.title: Where cards are built
workflow.option.followRemote.desc: Before each test merge, the merge queue fetches the remote branch the target tracks and tests on its latest commit, pushes each merge there only if nobody pushed meanwhile (testing again if they did), and then brings the local target up to date.
workflow.option.followRemote.title: The target branch follows its remote
workflow.option.identity.desc: Commits are made with the name and email from the project’s git config (else your global one).
workflow.option.identity.title: Commits use the project’s identity
workflow.option.loopRounds.desc: How many rounds a card gets in a card loop (a build and its review each) before its agents stop and ask you, when the loop doesn’t say.
workflow.option.loopRounds.title: Rounds
workflow.option.loopStepWaitMinutes.desc: How many minutes, up to 4 hours, a card loop’s builder waits for its reviewer to check a design it posted before it goes ahead as posted.
workflow.option.loopWaitHours.desc: How many hours, up to a day, an agent in a card loop waits with no change before it tells you, when the loop doesn’t say.
workflow.option.loopWaitHours.title: Wait (hours)
workflow.option.loopWakes.desc: When a card with a reviewer arrives in Review, Combwork wakes the reviewer, and on the review’s verdict the card’s builder; off, only the agents’ own card watches wake them.
workflow.option.loopWakes.title: Wake reviewers and builders
workflow.option.maxAgents.desc: Your team size: the most agents this project has, whoever adds them (you, the Assistant or a program using the Agent API), and lowering it removes none.
workflow.option.maxAgents.title: Maximum agents
workflow.option.mergeChecks.desc: Combwork’s merge queue runs these named commands on the card’s work merged with the target branch, and moves the target only once each one has passed.
workflow.option.mergeChecks.title: Checks pass on the merged result
workflow.option.mergeInstall.desc: Before the checks on the merged result, the merge queue installs the dependencies afresh, and always does when the lock file or manifests changed.
workflow.option.mergeInstall.title: Install dependencies from scratch
workflow.option.noSelfReview.desc: Always on while a reviewer agent checks the work.
workflow.option.noSelfReview.title: Nobody reviews their own work
workflow.option.okBefore.desc: A card waits for your OK before it is merged: never, only cards with these labels, or every card.
workflow.option.okBefore.title: Your OK before merging
workflow.option.otherTargets.desc: Branches a lane or a card can merge into instead (its Merges into), each through its own merge queue with the same merge checks, separated by commas.
workflow.option.otherTargets.title: Other branches work can merge into
workflow.option.preChecks.desc: A card goes to review only once each of these named commands has passed on its work.
workflow.option.preChecks.title: Checks pass before review
workflow.option.pushTarget.desc: After each merge, the merge queue pushes the target branch to the remote it tracks (or the only remote, or origin), never forced, and pauses, saying why, when the push is refused or fails.
workflow.option.pushTarget.title: Push the target branch after merging
workflow.option.review.desc: A card goes to Review when its builder submits it and moves on only once it passes, waiting for your OK after the reviewer when you check too.
workflow.option.review.none: Who checks the work before it’s done
workflow.option.review.shared: Work is reviewed before it’s done
workflow.option.review.title: Work is reviewed before it’s merged
workflow.option.reviewerMode.desc: One reviewer per lane, or a shared pool: Combwork gives each card submitted in a pool lane, oldest first, to the next free reviewer that didn’t build it.
workflow.option.reviewerMode.title: Reviewers
workflow.option.reviewers.desc: With two, both must pass the same change.
workflow.option.reviewers.title: Reviewers per card
workflow.option.sameness.desc: With Same change, a pass carries over to a clean rebase or squash of the same change; with Exact revision only, any new revision makes it stale.
workflow.option.sameness.title: A pass survives a clean rebase
workflow.option.sharedFolderWarning.desc: A submit warns, never refuses, when its commit takes in files another agent is editing in the project folder.
workflow.option.sharedFolderWarning.titl: Warn when a commit includes another agent’s files
workflow.option.slotsUpToDate.desc: Before a card starts in a slot, the slot is brought to the latest work of the target branch, and its dependencies are installed again when the lock file changed.
workflow.option.slotsUpToDate.title: Slots are brought up to date before each card
workflow.option.stageNames.desc: Rename any stage the board shows: a name changes no rule and applies at once.
workflow.option.stageNames.title: Stage names
workflow.option.stopOwnRuns.desc: A card goes to review only once its builder’s own runs and background commands have stopped.
workflow.option.stopOwnRuns.title: Agents stop what they started before review
workflow.option.strict.desc: When the target branch has moved on since the review, the merge queue brings the work up to date in its own folder first, and returns the card if that conflicts or makes a different change.
workflow.option.strict.title: Work is up to date with its target branch before it merges
workflow.option.style.desc: How a card’s work is merged into the target branch.
workflow.option.style.title: Merge style
workflow.option.target.desc: The branch a card’s work is merged into: the repository’s default branch when left empty.

workflow.why.commitMessage: Card titles can name people and details a public history shouldn’t keep; choose Combwork’s for the card’s key, linking each merge to its card.
workflow.why.dependenciesDone: It’s cheap, and no card is built on work that isn’t in yet.
workflow.why.excluded: Dependencies and build output aren’t part of what a card delivers.
workflow.why.finish: Merged through Combwork’s queue, red work never reaches the target branch; working solo, a card is done once it’s committed.
workflow.why.focusedTests: Each card’s own tests on the merged result catch what its change breaks there, without running every test for every card.
workflow.why.folder: Pairs and teams build in parallel, each card apart from the others.
workflow.why.followRemote: Following a remote reaches it and its sign-in before every merge, so it stays yours unless you turn it on.
workflow.why.identity: Commits name the project’s identity, whoever’s computer made them.
workflow.why.maxAgents: Each preset is for a team of its size (one agent solo, a builder and a reviewer as a pair), so the Assistant never adds agents you didn’t plan for.
workflow.why.mergeChecks: The checks run on the work as it will be once merged, not only as it was built.
workflow.why.mergeInstall: A clean install before every merge catches a dependency that only worked on the builder’s machine.
workflow.why.noSelfReview: A builder never passes its own work.
workflow.why.okBefore: Some work needs your eyes before it ships, such as screenshots and release steps.
workflow.why.preChecks: Cheap checks before review catch most of the rounds that would be lost, and a team adds its tests.
workflow.why.pushTarget: Pushing reaches your remote and its sign-in, so it stays yours unless you turn it on.
workflow.why.review: A pair exists to review: a second agent catches what the builder missed, while working solo you read the card’s work yourself.
workflow.why.reviewerMode: One reviewer per lane keeps the work with a reviewer who has seen its earlier rounds; a shared pool suits a large team.
workflow.why.reviewers: One reviewer is enough for most work; a second doubles the cost.
workflow.why.sameness: A clean rebase doesn’t change what was reviewed, so the pass still counts.
workflow.why.sharedFolderWarning: In a shared folder, one agent’s commit can take in another’s half-done files.
workflow.why.slotsUpToDate: Each card starts from the latest work, so no card is built on an old copy of the target branch.
workflow.why.stopOwnRuns: A run left going would keep changing or testing the work under review.
workflow.why.strict: The merge queue tests the merged result anyway, so this mostly changes the history’s shape.
workflow.why.style: A merge commit keeps each card’s own commits, as Combwork has always merged.
workflow.why.target: Finished work goes to the repository’s default branch; working solo, to the branch the project is on.
